name: @clossys/bouncer
description: The bouncer role: is this actor who they claim, and is what they are doing still inside what they were granted? Dependency-free machinery for a consumer's own authority records: a closed consumer-declared role hierarchy, a fail-closed session predicate, external-membership reconciliation against a provider of record, a strict redirect allowlist, an isolated ./agent subpath for delegated machine actors, provider adapters isolated behind ./providers/* so the root stays provider-neutral, a runtime verdict that is a ternary — authorized, denied, unverifiable — because a provider that did not answer is neither of the other two, and three gates behind one bouncer-check bin: authority-reconciliation, which fails when a live grant is revoked upstream, is not backed by its provider of record at all, or has passed its own declared expiry, and which exits 2 rather than 0 when a provider could not be reached; delegation-ceiling, which fails when a machine actor has no declared spend ceiling, has an undeclared unlimited one, has an amount with no currency or a currency with no amount, names no responsible human, or has an empty tool scope; and provider-contract, which fails when an adapter reads a field or recognises an event the provider no longer declares, requires a field the provider only sometimes sends, or ignores an event the provider does emit. Ships the schema and the checkers; every consumer authors its own values.
author: Calvin Hung
